newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Brent/Dubai spread narrows, but wider than $2.00.
newsitem.headline: Brent/Dubai spread narrows, but wider than $2.00.

text.p: The Brent/Dubai spread for November held above the $2.00 level in Asia on Tuesday in the wake of the Brent futures slide overnight.
Dubai intermonths were steady and the fall on Tapis paper was limited, traders said.
November Brent/Dubai was quoted at $2.08/$2.20, in 15-20 cents from London levels. December was quoted at $1.93/$2.05.
Brokers said there was interest to trade the spread despite the overnight volatility on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) and NYMEX.
November Brent futures slumped $1.53 to $21.60 in London in a correction from the Iraq-related rally and on reports that the United States had asked Saudi Arabia to produce more oil.
A Gulf source said Saudi Arabia was strictly abiding by its OPEC quota of 8.0 million barrels per day (bpd) and denied that the U.S. had asked the exporter to hike output.
On SIMEX, November Brent last traded at $21.84 in a bounce from the overnight losses.
November/December was assessed at 37/43, December/January at 35/42 and January/February at 35/41, little changed from the day-earlier.
October paper Tapis was quoted at $21.75/$21.95 early afternoon in Singapore, down from $22.00/$22.30 late on Monday after the Brent slide had started in London.
Traders said the Tapis market was holding up well despite the crude futures decline, which they attributed to underlying support for wet, light-sweet regional crudes.
